The word "loss" is definitional and its boundary is contested by design.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Loss expressly excludes claim expenses, while Article V allocates claim expenses by the ratio of loss borne — so the definition drives Article V and can produce a zero-denominator or zero-share result. That interaction is a plausible source of internal strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All payments under the supplementary payments provisions of the REINSURED'S policy, including court costs, interest upon judgments, and allocated investigation, adjustment, and legal expenses" is a general phrase followed by an illustrative list, leaving unclear whether items such as declaratory-judgment or coverage-litigation costs fall within it. The word "allocated" is itself undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against Article IV's carve-out of employee salaries and statutory penalties and against Article V's pro-rata indemnity, and the fit of "supplementary payments" language borrowed from the underlying policy into a reinsurance treaty is not seamless. A moderate relational question exists.

The proviso also refers to "such settlement or appeal" though no settlement was previously mentioned.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The formula depends entirely on the Article IV definitions of "loss" and "claim expenses," and Article IX's grant of participation "at its own expense" cuts across who bears defence costs. That combination is a plausible source of dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I covers Automobile Liability with a $1,000,000 underlying limit, and this pricing rule presumes no separate charge in most cases, which is a rating rather than coverage matter. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The entry reads "-125" and "25" with no units and "excluding BPL" is likely a typo for PL; the meaning must be inferred. Modest mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The nursing home and facility sections of the same schedule state the analogous factor as ".25" and ".15," creating apparent inconsistency in the figures. Modest.
judgments.clause_name: Rating Schedule-B - Indiana and Wisconsin Factor

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The ladder gives 35% credit for both the 2nd and 3rd years, while the corresponding Schedule-A ladder gives 45% and 35% — an apparent transcription error in a numeric term. Nameable mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs from the superseded Schedule-A ladder, which is permissible for an amendment, and nothing else fixes claims-made credits. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Apply a 1.30 factor to the Mature Claims-Made premium" with a three-year conversion period and a free extended reporting endorsement is mechanically stated, though "the conversion period will be three years" leaves the start date implicit. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the "claims-conversion basis" added to Article I by Amendment No. 4 and interacts with the discovery-period sentence in Article I. Low to modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two credits, each tied to a stated class, with an express carve-out for minimum premiums. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the minimum premium tables that follow. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 15% factor is applied to "OHIC's Manual GL and Professional Liability Premium (before application of experience and schedule rating)," a defined base, and the auto loads are fixed dollar amounts. Largely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to the reinsured by its former name OHIC, which Amendment No. 3 substituted, so the reference is coherent; nothing conflicts. Low.
judgments.clause_name: Rating Schedule-B - Nursing Home Rating Rates

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A discretionary schedule credit or debit "at the REINSURED'S discretion but not to exceed 25% for a credit" caps the credit but leaves debits uncapped and the discretion unqualified. That asymmetry is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same discretion appears in the facility rating section and does not conflict with Article VI's minimum premium requirement. Low.
judgments.clause_name: Rating Schedule-B - Nursing Home Rating Credits

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bullet labels and the percentage figures are printed in separate blocks and the "Minimum Premiums" heading is embedded mid-list, so the pairing of layer to factor depends on reading order. Modest mechanical risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Amendment No. 4's $10,000,000 nursing home limit, which the nine excess factors track. Low.
judgments.clause_name: Rating Schedule-B - Nursing Home Excess Factors

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Each million in limits is subject to a minimum premium of $1,000,000" is on its face absurd for a layer whose limit is $1,000,000 and is almost certainly a misplaced figure. That is a clear mechanical error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Every other minimum premium table in the schedules states figures in the thousands, confirming the inconsistency with the rest of the instrument. Moderate.
judgments.clause_name: Rating Schedule-B - Nursing Home Minimum Premiums

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The entries "25" and "258" are given without units or decimal points and the heading says "excluding PIL," a likely typo; the meaning cannot be read off the text. Mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The hospital section of the same schedule gives "-125" and "25" for the same items, so the figures do not line up across sections. Modest.
judgments.clause_name: Rating Schedule-B - Nursing Home Indiana and Wisconsin Factor

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 25% factor applied to a defined manual premium base with fixed auto loads; the "$ 80.00 for each private passenger vehicle" differs from the nursing home section's $50.00 but each is stated plainly. Largely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the nursing home rating section and supports the outpatient facility coverage added by Amendment No. 4. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Per-$1,000-of-receipts rates by layer, plainly stated, with a cross-reference to "the preceding paragraph" for autos that is slightly loose. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the facility rating structure and with the ten-million tower contemplated by the amended Article III. Low.
judgments.clause_name: Rating Schedule-B - Facility Rating Imaging (MRI) Risks

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same capped-credit-but-uncapped-debit discretion as the nursing home version, exercised at OHIC's discretion. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors the nursing home rating credit provision; no conflict. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean descending ladder of percentages tied to named layers. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the $10,000,000 outpatient facility limit in the amended Article III. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The first million is subject to a minimum premium of $1,500,000" states a minimum premium exceeding the limit it buys — a plain arithmetic impossibility and an evident misplaced figure. Clear mechanical error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is out of line with every other minimum premium table in the schedules, which run in the low thousands. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The factor is printed as "-is" with no readable numeral, so the term cannot be applied as written. Mechanical defect on the face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel entries elsewhere in Schedule-B give ".125" and ".25" for the same item, so the three sections do not agree. Modest.
judgments.clause_name: Rating Schedule-B - Facility Indiana and Wisconsin Factor

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Terminated with respect to loss under policies issued on or after January 1, 1998" is a precise cut-off keyed to policy issuance rather than to loss date or occurrence date. Largely definite, though "issued" versus "becoming effective" (Article I's phrase) is a small mismatch.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XI's termination machinery requires 90 days' notice and continues in-force policies to natural expiry up to twelve months plus odd time, and it uses "becoming effective" rather than "issued"; reconciling this stipulation with that run-off is a specific question.
